summary: Add a named parseBytes(string) export to pretty-bytes, the reverse of prettyBytes. Binary units are committed. Decimal units are in the code, but different branches want them read differently.
narrative: The owner asked for parseBytes on the branch the storage web app pins: plain numbers and KiB to YiB, with tests and types. The agent built it, fixed xo lint and doc-example test failures, and committed 71491a6 (#3-#8). The owner then said the storage team wants units without the i read as 1024 (Windows Explorer style), to be added later. A second conversation, on the branch the billing service pins, asked for the same export. It asked for strict SI, so 1 MB is 1,000,000 bytes. The agent added SI units as powers of 1000 and committed 585ae6a (#13-#15). A third conversation asked to finish kB/KB, MB, GB and the rest and to document them in the readme. The agent extended the unit table to SI (1000-based, KB as an alias for kB), updated the docs, fixed two lint errors, and got 58 tests passing (#18-#20). The 1000-based reading conflicts with the storage branch's 1024 requirement. Nothing is merged or released, and the third conversation's work has no recorded commit.

milestones.text: Owner asked for parseBytes (plain numbers and binary units, tests and types) for the storage web app branch; decimal units deferred.
xo lint and doc-example test failures fixed; ava passes with 55 tests.
Owner said the storage team wants non-i units read as powers of 1024, to be added next time.
Billing-service branch asked for the same export, requiring strict SI (1 MB = 1,000,000 bytes) for the later units.
SI units added as 1000-based and committed as 585ae6a; 58 tests pass.
Owner asked to finish the non-i units and document them; SI parsing, docs and tests done with 58 tests passing, no commit recorded.

preferences.preference: Wants tests and types delivered with new features.
Wants scope kept narrow, with open questions deferred rather than guessed.
preferences.quote: Leave out kB/MB/GB and friends for now; I still have to check with the storage team how they want those read.
